exam_facts.result: Multiple skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities
Lesions are firm, without warmth or erythema
Optional and not typically necessary. Could show lobules of molluscum bodies (Henderson-Paterson bodies) in the epidermis, if performed.

Sodium 138 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, chloride 104 mmol/L, bicarbonate 22 mmol/L, BUN 6 mg/dL, creatinine 0.3 mg/dL, glucose 82 mg/dL, ALT 18 U/L, AST 20 U/L, total bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL, albumin 4.1 g/dL

Color: pale yellow; clarity: clear; pH: 6.0; specific gravity: 1.012; protein: negative; glucose: negative; ketones: negative; leukocyte esterase: negative; nitrites: negative; RBC: 0–1/HPF; WBC: 0–2/HPF; no casts or crystals

exam_facts.test: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) PCR from skin swab of a non-umbilicated papule (for differential of HSV folliculitis or eczema herpeticum)
Streptococcus pyogenes rapid antigen test (throat swab)
Tinea fungal culture (from scale scraped from lesion edge)
Syphilis serology (RPR and confirmatory Treponema pallidum IgG EIA)
exam_facts.result: RPR nonreactive (titer <1:1); T. pallidum IgG EIA negative

Normal liver echotexture, no focal lesions; gallbladder without wall thickening or stones; kidneys symmetric with preserved corticomedullary differentiation; no lymphadenopathy in mesentery or retroperitoneum; no cutaneous/subcutaneous mass effect corresponding to skin lesions
